en.text: Barteria fistulosa is a species of tree in the family Passifloraceae, native to tropical Central Africa. The tree has an association with an aggressive species of ant with a very painful sting, which lives in its hollow branches and twigs, and gives rise to its common name of "ant tree".

fr.text: Barteria fistulosa est une espèce de plantes à fleurs de la famille des Passifloraceae. C'est un arbuste à tronc creux vivant dans les forêts équatoriales en Afrique centrale. Il vit, entre autres, en symbiose avec des fourmis du genre Tetraponera.

en.heading: Uses
en.text: Several parts of this tree are used in traditional medicine; the roots, bark and leaves are used to reduce fevers and pains; a decoction of the bark has various uses and the sap helps with the healing of wounds; some parts of the tree are used against snake bites and epilepsy; and the young shoots are thought to have aphrodisiac properties.
